### B1 — the nightly constructive set at 10 draws (C-0227 (13): 100)

* Executed in the derive mirror. Script: `nightlyJobs()` / `milestoneJobs()`, then the B-FUZZ job's units, then the
  constants of `bench/src/fuzz-bar/index.ts`:
  `nightly 25 units; first: fuzz-bar --primitive insertChain --runs 1000000 --constructive-seeds 10 --no-summary | last: fuzz-bar --runs 1 --constructive-seeds 10 --no-summary`
  (the milestone list is identical) · `fuzz-bar CONSTRUCTIVE_SEEDS_PR 10 CONSTRUCTIVE_SEEDS_NIGHTLY 100`.
* What the harness does: `fuzz-bar/index.ts:135` reads `perCase = seeds ?? (runs >= 1_000_000 ? CONSTRUCTIVE_SEEDS_NIGHTLY : CONSTRUCTIVE_SEEDS_PR)`.
  The nightly's `constructive set` unit passes `--runs 1 --constructive-seeds 10`, so it runs the PR's 10 draws. The
  harness's own comment (l. 48) calls 100 "the nightly's … (C-0227 (13))". C-0227 (13) reads: "the bench runs every M0
  case at 10 draws in the PR tier and 100 at the nightly size".
* `index.ts:60,63` hard-codes `PR_CONSTRUCTIVE_DRAWS` for every tier. `units.test.ts` ("B-FUZZ at 10⁶ per primitive …")
  pins `'--constructive-seeds', '10'` for the nightly, so the test holds the narrowed size in place. C-0460 (3) calls
  this "the constructive set at its fixed draws (`--constructive-seeds 10`)". C-0460 says it "refines nothing;
  supersedes nothing", so it leaves C-0227 (13) in force.
* **Required change:** `fuzzUnits` takes the tier's draws. The PR keeps 10. The nightly and milestone pass 100
  (`CONSTRUCTIVE_SEEDS_NIGHTLY`, read from the harness, not retyped) on the `constructive set` unit, and on the
  `--primitive` units if those keep the flag. `units.test.ts` pins 100 for the nightly and milestone and 10 for the PR.
  The fallback still never cuts the constructive set.

### B2 — the `suites` declarations unpinned (§13.8 *Edges*; C-0460 (2); `M0-f-02a-notes.md` N-6)

* Mutants (each run first on NEAR, the 4 files at full strength with `--maxWorkers=1`, then on RELATED@1000; baseline
  RELATED `5 failed | 168 passed (173)`):
  * X01: drop `suites: [FUSION_FIXTURE]` from `fusion spike (full seed set)`. Result: `48 passed (48)` and `5 failed | 168 passed (173)`. SURVIVED.
  * X02: drop it from `site spike (full seed set)`. SURVIVED, same counts.
  * X03: drop it from `bent-cut F-CUT harness`. SURVIVED.
  * X04: drop it from `F-CUT (10⁵ faces)`. SURVIVED.
  * X05: drop the parity job's `{ kind: 'seeds', path: PARITY_OURS }`. SURVIVED.
  * Killed for comparison: X06 (the PR site stand-in's suite: `units.test.ts` names it) and X07 (the cross-host
    suite: its path appears nowhere else, so the set-of-paths test misses it).
* Why they survive: `lists.test.ts` "a built spike job whose fixture suite is missing or empty fails naming it"
  iterates `.filter((x) => (x.suites ?? []).length > 0 && x.inputs.length === 0)`, so a job without a declaration is
  never asked. "every declared suite exists …" compares the SET of paths across all tiers. The PR fusion job still
  carries `flat.ts` and the nightly bent cut still carries `faces.ts`, so a nightly or milestone job can lose its
  suite unseen. The parity job is excluded from both tests because of its `inputs`.
* Without the declaration, an emptied `flat.ts` no longer fails the nightly fusion job "naming it" before a unit runs
  (§13.8: "a suite whose seed family, fixture set or baseline file is empty or missing fails naming it"). The mutants
  are not equivalent.
* **Required change:** a test pins each job's `suites` exactly, as a table of job name → suites over all three
  tiers, parity's our side included. The empty-suite test runs over that expected list, not over whichever jobs
  happen to declare a suite. The parity job's suite is exercised with `baselines.json` and both reviews planted in the
  fixture tree.

### B3 — the hang attribution's replay and wiring unpinned (routed row x-06:19 (10))

* Mutants on `bench/src/tier-jobs/cli.ts`, each SURVIVED on NEAR (`48 passed`) and RELATED (`5 failed | 168 passed`):
  * X22: `main`'s `edge-hangs` passes `seeds: 10` instead of `edgeSeedCount()`. At the nightly, a hang at seed 11+
    then reads "no hang — its unit's own failure".
  * X23: `edgeReplay` iterates seeds `1..n` instead of `edgeSeeds(id, n)`. It replays the wrong family and names a
    wrong seed or none.
  * X24: `replayFixture`'s default argv passes `'1'` instead of `String(seeds)`, so one seed is replayed.
  * X25: `edgeReplay` returns at the first throwing seed instead of continuing, so a hang after a throw is never
    reached.
  * X30: `main` passes `EDGE_FIXTURES.slice(0, 5)`. The other 67 built fixtures are never checked against the logs,
    and the unit exits 0 "no unattributed hang".
* Why they survive: `cli.test.ts` drives `edgeHangs` with an injected `seeds` and `replay`, and `replayFixture` with
  an injected `argv`. `edgeReplay` (the child) and the `edge-hangs` branch of `main` have no test.
* The probe today (CONFIRMED in the derive mirror): `cli.ts edge-replay EP-04/S5c 2` printed
  `{"start":1110161637}` `{"done":1110161637,"ms":1210}` `{"start":3221545785}` `{"done":3221545785,"ms":710}`,
  which equals `edgeSeeds(EP-04/S5c, 2) = [1110161637,3221545785]`. With `PLAT_EDGE_SEEDS=1000`,
  `edgeSeedCount() = 1000`, with 72 built fixtures of 129. `edge-hangs` over an empty out folder printed
  `tier-jobs edge-hangs: no edge-suite log under …: the edge units wrote none` and exited 1. The code is right
  today; what is missing is the pin the routed row asks this build for ("each becomes a nightly-tier job or check
  with its pin").
* **Required change:** tests that hold these behaviours:
  * `edgeReplay`'s seeds equal `edgeSeeds(id, n)` and it continues past a throwing seed (with an injectable fixture
    list, or the real list on one fixture at n = 2);
  * `replayFixture`'s default command line carries the fixture and n;
  * `main(['edge-hangs', …])` hands `edgeHangs` the whole `EDGE_FIXTURES` and `edgeSeedCount()` (for example through
    an injectable `ctx`, or with logs planted for every built fixture but one, asserting the replay request).

### B4 — a cap-only receipt's PARTIAL label unpinned (the session's receipt rule)

* Mutant X40: `const partial = rm.sampled.length > 0;` (the `|| capMs !== null` dropped). SURVIVED on NEAR and on
  RELATED. `summary.test.ts`'s receipt test always passes `--sample` together with `--unit-cap-ms`, and the test of the
  bare receipt passes neither.
* What the mutant does: `receipt --tier T --unit-cap-ms N` wraps every unit in the cap's `watch` (stopped at N,
  exit 124), but writes `receipt: 'whole'`, `partial: null` into the summary. That is a wrong committed result, and
  the receipt rule exists to prevent it ("marks that tier's receipt PARTIAL with the reason").
* Today's code is right. A probe test in the derive mirror (not in the tree) ran `main(['receipt', '--tier',
  'nightly', '--unit-cap-ms', '60000', …])` over a fixture tree with a planted executor and passed, with
  `receipt: 'PARTIAL'`. The fault is the missing pin.
* **Required change:** a test of a cap-only receipt. Its section reads `PARTIAL`, and its reason names the cap and
  "every job whole".
